name: AGC 239141 (Hubble)
blurb: AGC 239141, a low-mass irregular galaxy, seen by Hubble.
label: agc239141-hubble
story: Hubble split this small galaxy into individual stars to measure its distance from the tip of its red giant branch. It is one of twelve nearby low-mass galaxies chosen to test whether the link between a galaxy's mass and its rotation bends at the smallest masses.

claims.text: AGC 239141 is an irregular galaxy targeted by Hubble program 17480
The program's twelve targets are nearby Local Volume galaxies with low baryonic masses
Hubble measures their distances from the tip of the red giant branch
The program tests whether the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation (baryonic mass vs. rotation) bends at low masses
